SHORT_DESCRIPTION: RESTRUCTURE: ESKOM RENEWABLES SUPPORT PROJECT COMPONENT 2
PROJECT_TITLE: Restructure: Eskom Renewables Support Project Component 2
LONG_DESCRIPTION: The Project restructuring seeks to (1) replace the 'Kiwano' (Upington) Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) Plant' pilot project with a large-scale distributed Battery Storage Program1 linked to continuation of South Africa's Renewable Energy Independent Power Producers (REIPP) Program. It also seeks to (2) reallocate the remaining proceeds from the completed activities to the battery storage investment program and (3) extend the project implementation period until December 30, 2021, to allow sufficient time for successful implementation of this storage program.The proposed changes to the project components involve a change of activity in component 2 to include financing for grid-scale distributed electrochemical batteries, to complement the operation of new wind and solar power capacity to be built under REIPPP round 4, Sere wind farm financed under the Project, and with future distributed solar PV capacity to be built and operated by Eskom.A technical assistance sub-component under component 2 will be added to (i) support the final design, procurement and supervision of energy storage infrastructure to be supplied through the project, (ii) to strengthen Eskom technical capacity in sustainable operation and maintenance of large scale batteries and (iii) to prepare the enabling environment (regulatory, technical, construction standards) for further private investment in VRE capacity using storage.

The project will install BettaFour solar light kits in the homes of community members, altogether 130 households in Kwadlakuse and Esikhuthwaneni, two deeply rural villages in Northern KwaZulu-Natal, which is one of the poorest regions in South Africa largely due to its history as a marginalised homeland. Access to electricity is important for the rural poor as it reduces especially women's work burden, improve people's standards of living and children's educational outcomes. Earlier the households have met their energy needs using fossil fuels and/or biomass. Project will contribute to climate change mitigation, as fossil fuels will be replaced by solar power. Project's solar kits were selected as they offer a practical and cost effective way to provide light to rural households living in isolated areas. The system consists of four 1 watt LED lights, a controller with lead crystal battery, a 10 watt solar panel and a 10Ah 6 Volt Lead crystal battery. Solar power provides communities lightning without costs.The installation will involve members from each household and basic training on the use of the unit will be provided to promote long term sustainability. Each household will also be required to sign a social contract which explains that (unless defective) the property becomes their responsibility. In addition to overseeing the installation of the lighting kits, ACT mentors will provide assistance in the development of homestead food gardens, as well as offer advice in ways to store and save water when they visit the households. The proposed project will be four months in duration and budget is inclusive of all equipment, administration costs and tax. Monitoring will take place throughout the project and periodic visits will also be conducted by ACT teams once the project has been completed. The project aimed to work in conjunction with the three communities bordering the reserve to develop an environmentally, socially and economically beneficial plan to expand the protected area. The two communities in this project take part in the Mkuze River project.

From June 11-19, the AIDO hosted a tripartite delegation from South Africa. The delegation was comprised of stakeholders from the Petroleum Authority of South Africa, the Department of Mineral Resources and the Mine, Health and Safety Council of South Africa. The delegation embarked on a capacity building program in the fields of drilling, facilities management, health, safety and environmental components as part of their readiness plan for monitoring shale gas activities and petroleum development activities in general. Purpose of the visit was to  have a two-year long skills transfer programme in the fields of drilling, facilities management, health, safety and environmental management with the Canadian regulatory authorities tasked with providing the regulatory oversight and monitoring of the activities. The AIDO coordinated and facilitated a program in Calgary and in Edmonton, including site visits and a session with the key Government of Alberta Ministries. The delegation has already submitted a proposal on how to proceed with the Alberta institutions they engaged.
